correctness.rationale: Explicit full seven-state and reduced three-/five-state generators independently agree. Cramer resolvent identities and the determinant factorization are proved algebraically; positivity follows from transient-generator M-matrix determinants and a strictly positive polynomial. Mean and fifth-order statements follow from s=0 and generator-power expansions. The actual package checker passed 100 symbolic/exact rational assertions; finite examples alone are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The full text of Gilarranz–Bascompte 2011 online, Barbillon et al. 2014, Grilli et al. 2015, and the relevant contact-process theorem in Mountford et al. 2012 was compared on dynamics, objective, topology and budget. Earlier results either use discrete-time schemes, large-network stochastic averages, deterministic spectral thresholds or asymptotic lifetimes. Their statements do not imply the fixed-sum-edge-rate three-patch strict Laplace-transform comparison; ordinary edgewise attractiveness does not apply because path edge rates exceed triangle rates. Searches do not establish historical uniqueness, and an unindexed finite-state calculation is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An old numerical, reliability or finite-state Markov-chain source may contain the identical three-node fixed-budget computation under different terminology.
Search coverage and accessible full texts cannot prove global uniqueness.
No claim is made for deterministic-time stochastic order or for larger graphs.

value.rationale: A fixed total edge-intensity budget makes topology comparisons nontrivial: the triangle uses three weaker connections, the corridor two stronger ones. The result determines the entire exponential-deadline persistence ordering at the minimal nontrivial connected network size for every rate, plus a concrete relative asymptotic gain of 32/27 and delayed fifth-order onset. This is a motivated finite ecological network benchmark, not a routine fixed-rate edge-addition comparison.
